Package dev.shvquu.betternpcs.api.action

Klasse BuiltinActions

java.lang.Object
dev.shvquu.betternpcs.api.action.BuiltinActions
public final class BuiltinActions extends Object
The ids of the action handlers BetterNPCs registers itself.

Referencing a constant from here instead of writing the string keeps a typo a compile error, and makes it obvious which ids an extension must not try to claim.

Seit:
1.0.0

    • TITLE

      public static final String TITLE
      Shows a title to the interacting player.

      The argument is the title and the subtitle separated by |, either of which may be empty.

      Example: title: <gold>Welcome|<gray>to the shop

      Siehe auch:
      • Konstantenfeldwerte

    • PLAYER_COMMAND

      public static final String PLAYER_COMMAND
      Runs the argument as a command, as the interacting player.

      The command runs with the player's own permissions — this action cannot be used to give a player access to something they could not already run themselves. Use CONSOLE_COMMAND when elevated rights are the point.

      Example: command: spawn

      Siehe auch:
      • Konstantenfeldwerte

    • CONSOLE_COMMAND

      public static final String CONSOLE_COMMAND
      Runs the argument as a command from the console.

      Runs with full permissions, so an NPC carrying this action is as powerful as the person who configured it. Editing NPC actions is therefore gated behind betternpcs.action.console separately from the general edit permission.

      Example: console: give <player_name> diamond 1

      Siehe auch:
      • Konstantenfeldwerte

    • SOUND

      public static final String SOUND
      Plays a sound to the interacting player.

      The argument is a sound key, optionally followed by a volume and a pitch separated by spaces.

      Example: sound: entity.player.levelup 1.0 1.2

    • COOLDOWN

      public static final String COOLDOWN
      Stops the rest of the chain if the player has interacted with this NPC too recently.

      The argument is the cooldown in seconds. Placing it first in a chain is how an NPC is protected against click spam.

      Example: cooldown: 3
